calibration.dev_correct_pool: every calibration row the frozen 122 path routes AND answers correctly (verdict CORRECT): 388 rows (heldout122 + exp99 + exp100 + panels 105/114/122)
calibration.dev_wrong_pool: every calibration row the frozen 122 path answers WRONGLY (verdict WRONG): 49 rows (46 heldout122 + 3 panel122); panels 99/100/105/114 contribute 0 wrongs
calibration.note: heldout122 rows are the author's own train-adjacent phrasings (same styles as the bank); blind-panel rows are other-agent phrasings, distribution-matched to the fresh blind panel. The rule uses both pools exactly as stated, with no per-intent hand-tuning.

intents_without_delta_note: no correctly-routed calibration row exists for these labels (their answers are always the decline sentence), so the guard is vacuous for them: decline iff 1 - max-cosine > +inf, i.e. never. This changes no verdict.
rule: ONE fixed rule, applied identically to every content intent L in C1..C30: delta_L = min( max NN cosine distance over the dev_correct_pool rows routed to L, PLUS a fixed keep-side margin 1e-4, min NN cosine distance over the dev_wrong_pool rows from BLIND panels routed to L, MINUS a fixed epsilon 1e-6 ); where no blind-panel wrong was routed to L, delta_L = the max term plus 1e-4. Guard fires (decline) iff the question NN distance strictly exceeds delta_L. The 1e-4 margin covers measured cross-run float noise (<= 1.2e-7, from batch-1 vs batch-64 embedding) ~1000x, so rows defining the max keep are never flipped by noise; the 1e-6 epsilon keeps the three blind-panel wrongs (each exactly 1e-6 above its delta by construction) on the decline side with ~8x noise margin.
